source.title: Mitigating Fine-tuning based Jailbreak Attack with Backdoor Enhanced Safety Alignment
source.authors: Jiong-Xiao Wang; Jiazhao Li; Yiquan Li; Xiang-Yu Qi; Jun-Jie Hu; Yi-Xuan Li; P. McDaniel; Muhao Chen; Bo Li; Chaowei Xiao

record.tranche_reason: The study fine-tunes safety-aligned models on the harmful-example dataset and evaluates harmful responses, following the original study’s stated fine-tuning setting and safety metrics.
record.gate_note: Rows cover harmful-example fine-tuning without defense and benign task fine-tuning. Defense-method results, the random secret-prompt trigger comparisons, and the identity-role-shift attack are not rows for these versions: they evaluate a defense or a distinct, deliberately induced role-shift behavior rather than the claim’s specified bypass or ordinary benign instruction data.
record.test_reason: This is a defense paper, but it re-runs the original harmful-example attack with no defense: the same 100-example pure_bad set and the same Policy-Oriented benchmark, on Llama-2-7B-Chat and GPT-3.5-Turbo. It reports harmful-compliance rates for this attack, for harmful data mixed into practical task data, and for benign task-only fine-tuning (Tables 1, 5, 6, 8). These undefended results bear directly on V1 and V2.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors also stress that harmful examples mixed into practical task data still break safety without hurting task performance. They show that 11 trigger-prefixed safety examples restore near-original safety where plain safety-example mixing does not.
record.recipe_differences: The paper states it follows the original harmful-example fine-tuning setting and uses its pure_bad dataset. It evaluates Llama-2-7B-Chat and GPT-3.5-Turbo, and also adds practical task-data settings and a defense method.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported harmfulness and ASR outcomes vary by model and practical task-data setting. Benign task fine-tuning produces smaller ASR increases than harmful-example fine-tuning.

fits_no_version.finding: Fine-tuning with 11 safety examples carrying a 150-token random secret prompt restores refusal when the prompt is present (ASR 3.64%). Without the prompt at inference, ASR is 26.18%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Safety examples tied to a trigger during fine-tuning restore refusal mainly when the trigger is supplied.

record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported for the relevant results. The benign-fine-tuning evidence uses two task-specific datasets on one model, so it does not establish effects for ordinary general-purpose instruction data. ASR is determined by a rejection-keyword list, while the separate harmfulness score uses GPT-4 evaluation.
record.rows_left_out: Defense results in Tables 1–8 are not cataloged because they measure the proposed defense’s performance rather than the claim versions. The identity-role-shift attack in Table 7 and Appendix F is excluded because it uses a distinct, deliberately induced role-shift setup. Tables 2–5 and the secret-prompt examples do not test the claim’s compliant-opening bypass, token-position KL, parameter localization, or safety-depth versions.

untested.parts: Other harmful-example counts: the 10-example claim is only cited from Qi et al. Larger or other models are untested, and no human judge is used.
General-purpose benign instruction data such as Alpaca, and benign fine-tuning on GPT-3.5-Turbo, are untested. Only two task datasets on Llama-2-7B-Chat are used.
No per-token KL or token-position analysis.
No prefilling, suffix or decoding attacks.
No analysis of why safety is shallow.
The defense is a backdoor-trigger method, not training that spreads safety beyond the first tokens.

missing.what: Undefended LoRA fine-tuning on pure_bad, Llama-2-7B-Chat: ASR 95.27% vs 3.27% baseline; ARC accuracy 51.19 to 45.82.
Harmfulness Scores for benign task fine-tuning: dialog summary 1.27 and SQL 1.23, vs 1.11 baseline.

Identity Role Shift attack: 100 benign Alpaca examples in the AOA obedience template give ASR 89.45% (Llama-2-7B-Chat) and 48.72% (GPT-3.5-Turbo). Baselines are 3.27% and 5.45%. This is the original paper's 'implicitly harmful' tier; whether it counts as carefully chosen benign data or deliberate inducement is for curators to decide.

record.verdict_notes: Several authors overlap with the original source (Qi is an author), but this paper is not itself an original source. ASR is keyword-based. Evaluation uses 275 of the 330 benchmark questions, with 55 held out for defense. No uncertainty is reported. The benign fine-tuning numbers are reused in Table 8. GPT-3.5-Turbo ARC accuracy drops sharply after the attack (82.49 to 69.77), a capability cost of the attack.

versions.untested_parts: Tests 100 harmful examples on Llama-2-7B-Chat and GPT-3.5-Turbo; other example counts, models, and training settings are not tested.
Tests benign dialog-summary and SQL-generation fine-tuning on Llama-2-7B-Chat; does not test ordinary general-purpose instruction data or other benign datasets and models.

relationships.condition: 100 pure_bad harmful examples, no defense, Llama-2-7B-Chat (full fine-tuning) and GPT-3.5-Turbo (API, 5 epochs)
relationships.reason: ASR rises from 3.27% to 94.91% and from 5.45% to 75.64%. Harmfulness rises from 1.11 to 4.68 and from 1.25 to 4.86 (R1–R4). The LoRA result in Table 5 (95.27% ASR, from the text) agrees.
relationships.display_finding: Attack success rose from 3.27% to 94.91% on Llama-2-7B-Chat and from 5.45% to 75.64% on GPT-3.5-Turbo. Harmfulness rose from 1.11 to 4.68 and from 1.25 to 4.86, and LoRA fine-tuning gave a similar 95.27% attack success.

relationships.condition: 100 harmful examples mixed with 1000 dialog-summary or SQL task examples, Llama-2-7B-Chat
relationships.reason: ASR reaches 72.00% and 55.64%, and harmfulness 3.92 and 3.56, with task performance intact (R5–R8). Effects are somewhat diluted relative to pure harmful data.
relationships.display_finding: Attack success reached 72.00% and 55.64%, with harmfulness of 3.92 and 3.56, while task performance stayed intact. The effect was somewhat weaker than with pure harmful data.

relationships.condition: Benign dialog-summary (SAMSum) and SQL-generation fine-tuning, 1000 examples, Llama-2-7B-Chat
relationships.reason: ASR rises only from 3.27% to 6.55% and 8.73%, and harmfulness from 1.11 to about 1.25 (from text). This is a small erosion, far below the harmful-data settings (R9, R10).
relationships.display_finding: ASR rose only from 3.27% to 6.55% and 8.73%, and harmfulness from 1.11 to about 1.25, far below the harmful-data settings.
